facts.raw_span: intensely pruritic skin lesions on her anterior thighs
lesions first appeared 2 weeks earlier in recurrent 3‐day outbreaks
resolved spontaneously without residual injury
well‐defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology
central clearing, and purpuric edges
symmetrically distributed on the anterior thighs in a mirror‐image pattern
no systemic symptoms
no preceding infection
laboratory studies were within normal limits

complete blood count, biochemistry, urinalysis, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C‐reactive protein, complement levels (C3, C4, C1q), immunoglobulin levels, rheumatoid factor, and acute‐phase reactants were within normal limits
Antinuclear, anti–double‐stranded DNA, antineutrophil cytoplasmic, anti–Ro, anti–La, and transglutaminase antibodies were negative
Serologies for syphilis, hepatitis B and C viruses, HIV, cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, and parvovirus B19 were negative

concepts.why: The patient presents with intensely pruritic skin lesions, which is a hallmark symptom of urticaria.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic targetoid appearance, which is consistent with erythema multiforme.
The patient's skin lesions are symmetrically distributed on the anterior thighs, which could suggest an allergic reaction to a contact irritant.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic morphology, with annular and arciform shapes, which is consistent with pityriasis rosea.
The patient's skin lesions are well-defined and have a characteristic nummular appearance, which is consistent with nummular dermatitis.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic annular shape, which is consistent with annular erythema.

rationales.F01: Pruritic skin lesions are more typical of urticaria and annular erythema.
rationales.F02: Recurrent outbreaks are less typical of urticaria.
rationales.F04: Erythematous papules and plaques with annular morphology are more typical of erythema multiforme and annular erythema.
rationales.F05: Central clearing and purpuric edges are more typical of erythema multiforme and annular erythema.
rationales.F06: Symmetric distribution is more typical of erythema multiforme and contact dermatitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Annular Erythema best explains the well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, central clearing, and purpuric edges, as well as the symmetric distribution in a mirror-image pattern, without strong contradictions.
